communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Request for Proposal and Bid Submissions by all bidders for MetroHealth contract signed March 2023.
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The request for proposal and all resulting bid submissions and proposals sent by all bidders except for Experian, for the contract  eventually signed between MetroHealth and Experian on March 15, 2023, which covers Credit Reporting and Scoring, Financial Assistance Screening, PayNav or Propensity to Pay and Patient Financial Clearance. Please include all materials submitted by any and all companies, organizations, or entities seeking to win the contract, and include all documents submitted in relation to the following documents:

1. March 1, 2023, Document #00065213.0: MetroHealth - Master Customer Agreement & BAA  Experian Health CLEAN 3.1.2023_Stamped 
2. March 15, 2023, Document #00065213.0: Experian MSA, from 3.15.23

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Tracie McMillan

communications.subject: RE: Ohio Open Records Law Request- Acknowledgement
communications.communication:
Hello,



Your email to PublicRecords@MetroHealth.org<mailto:PublicRecords@MetroHealth.org> has been received. At MetroHealth, we strive to provide responses to public records requests promptly.  Please be aware that our response time will vary based on factors include the nature of the request and the number of requests under review at any given time.  To help make the process as efficient as possible, please provide as much clarity and detail as possible when submitting your request.



Also, please note, MetroHealth strictly adheres to its obligations under the Ohio Public Records law. MetroHealth also applies exemptions from disclosure as established by federal or state law, particularly where the laws are intended to protect the rights of third parties. When obligated by law, MetroHealth will withhold and/or redact any records that are specifically exempted from disclosure. Any such redactions or withholdings will be accompanied by a supporting explanation.



Generally, we return responses to public records requests by email at no charge. When a response by email is not practical, we may provide hardcopies by mail at a rate of 5 cents per page, or we may provide downloaded files to a compact disk at a rate of $1.00 per disk.



Finally, the email account, PublicRecords@MetroHealth.org<mailto:PublicRecords@MetroHealth.org>, is monitored closely during normal business hours, Monday through Friday from 7AM to 4PM. Please feel free to contact us with any questions or concerns you may have.
Thanks,

The Legal Department
The MetroHealth System
2500 MetroHealth Drive
Cleveland, Ohio 44109-1998

title: Consulate emails with AG (Office of the Attorney General - Nebraska)

communications.subject: Nebraska Public Records Act Request: Consulate emails with AG (Office of the Attorney General - Nebraska)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Emails, together with attachments, exchanged between May 1, 2022 and the date this request is received, between any employee or official of the Office of the Attorney General and any email address ending in "gov.il." The senders and recipients are identified above; the subject matter is communications between the Office and the government of Israel; the timeframe is stated above.

2. Records sufficient to show the search conducted for paragraph 1, including the accounts or custodians searched, the search terms or queries used, and the number of responsive items or hits located in each account.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status. If applicable, I request a waiver of all fees associated with this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Nessel MFA emails (older)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request all emails sent to or received from any address ending in “*.gov.il,” including any attachments, from 1 January 2019 to 6 October 2023, involving:
(1) Attorney General Dana Nessel; and
(2) whoever served, at any time during that period, in the following roles within the Attorney General's immediate executive office: Chief of Staff, Chief Deputy Attorney General, and Director of Communications / Public Information and Education (or the closest equivalent title if these positions have been renamed).

I do not have the names of every person who held these roles throughout the period, and ask that the Department identify and search the accounts of whoever occupied them at the relevant times. communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Consulate meetings
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Responses to two specific meeting requests.

Any communication sent by any Department employee in response to either of the following, including any reply, acknowledgment, scheduling message, declination, or referral to another person:

(a) the email from Hannah Giesen, Executive Secretary to Consul General Yinam Cohen, dated July 8, 2024, regarding a meeting in Detroit on July 23 or 24, 2024; and
(b) the email from Ethan Ramer, Senior Officer of Public Affairs, dated March 12, 2026, regarding a meeting in metro Detroit on March 13, 2026.
For this paragraph, please search all outbound communications sent between July 8, 2024 and August 31, 2024, and between March 12, 2026 and April 30, 2026, to the sender or to any address ending in "chicago.mfa.gov.il."

2. Scheduling records for the two relevant periods.

Existing calendar entries, meeting invitations, appointment records, invitations to events, and correspondence concerning the scheduling of any meeting or event involving the Attorney General, the Chief of Staff, the Chief Deputy Attorney General, or the Director of Communications / Office of Public Information and Education, for the following dates:

July 22, 23, and 24, 2024; and
March 12 and 13, 2026.
Please include, for each entry in that period, the identity of the invited or scheduled participants to the extent recorded.

3. Records of any meeting or event with the Consulate General.

Existing records — including briefing memoranda, agendas, talking points, readouts, follow-up correspondence, thank-you letters, and attendance or guest lists — concerning any meeting, event, reception, or conference attendance in which the Attorney General, or any official listed in paragraph 2, participated with the Consulate General of Israel to the Midwest or any of its officials or staff, between January 1, 2024 and the date this request is processed.

4. Records sufficient to show whether such a meeting occurred.

Existing records that reflect the outcome of paragraphs 1(a) and 1(b) or that record whether the Attorney General met with any representative of the Consulate General during the period covered by paragraph 3 — for example, a scheduling log, appointment list, or other existing record of meetings. I am not asking the Department to create a new record.

INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SEARCH

Please search for responsive records even if they are already publicly available. The Department should follow any leads it discovers during its searches and search additional systems or accounts where those leads indicate responsive records may be located. Records responsive to paragraphs 2 and 3 may be held in calendar, scheduling, or invitation systems rather than in email. Please search those systems, and search the accounts of any employee who maintained scheduling records for the officials listed in paragraph 2 during the relevant periods. I request disclosure of any and all supposedly "duplicate" pages.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
